subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway delays first-turn runtime plugin pre-warm beyond readiness

question: Should Gateway readiness be followed by immediate admitted runtime-plugin pre-warming, or should the current 10-second quiet window remain to protect post-ready event-loop responsiveness?
rationale: Both first-turn latency and post-ready event-loop saturation have real evidence, so the intended readiness-versus-warmth contract requires explicit maintainer ownership rather than an automatic timer change.

options.title: Pre-warm immediately after readiness
options.body: Schedule admitted, yielding, deduplicated registry preparation on the next event-loop opportunity and require readiness plus immediate-first-turn timing proof.

options.title: Include pre-warm in readiness
options.body: Keep first-turn latency out of the user path by delaying `/readyz` until the registry is prepared, accepting a longer reported startup time.

options.title: Keep the quiet window
options.body: Retain the 10-second delay and explicitly accept that immediate first turns may pay registry initialization cost.

recommendation.title: Pre-warm immediately after readiness
recommendation.body: Schedule admitted, yielding, deduplicated registry preparation on the next event-loop opportunity and require readiness plus immediate-first-turn timing proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal combines recent Gateway/runtime history with direct ownership of the live reproduction context.
